findings.claim: Q2 2026 free cash flow was negative USD 5.9bn — the first cash-negative quarter since the 2004 IPO — after capex doubled year on year to a record USD 44.9bn.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Alphabet Q2 2026 results; Tom's Hardware, FourWeekMBA, BigGo coverage

findings.claim: Alphabet repurchased no stock in the first half of 2026, against USD 28.3bn of buybacks in the same period a year earlier, with USD 69.5bn still authorised and unused.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: FourWeekMBA analysis of Q2 2026 capital allocation

findings.claim: Alphabet launched an USD 84.75bn equity raise — reported as the largest in US corporate history — to fund the AI infrastructure buildout through 2027, including a USD 10bn anchor investment from Berkshire Hathaway.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: FourWeekMBA; Motley Fool; Levelheaded Investing, Aug 2026

findings.claim: The company is simultaneously paying a dividend and issuing equity: a quarterly dividend of USD 0.22 per share payable 14 September 2026, raised 5% in April, costing roughly USD 10.8bn a year.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: Cash and securities stand at approximately USD 240bn against long-term debt of approximately USD 98bn, which has roughly doubled. Debt issuance proceeds were USD 64.56bn in 2025. Net cash is therefore approximately USD 142bn.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Simply Wall St; Eulerpool; Levelheaded Investing, 2026

findings.claim: This is a complete inversion of the capital structure policy. A company that returned roughly USD 70bn a year to shareholders is now raising debt and equity to fund capex, in the way a utility funds a grid buildout rather than the way a software company funds growth.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from the buyback halt, the equity raise and the debt increase

findings.claim: Q2 2026 other income was a net gain of USD 98.0bn, primarily unrealised gains on equity securities in SpaceX and a private company — an increase of USD 95.3bn year on year.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Alphabet Q2 2026 results / 10-Q as summarised in coverage

findings.claim: Alphabet itself quantified the distortion: the USD 99.0bn net gain on equity securities increased the tax provision by USD 21.9bn, net income by USD 77.1bn and diluted EPS by USD 6.26. Reported Q2 EPS of USD 9.11 therefore contains USD 2.85 of operating earnings and USD 6.26 of paper gain.
findings.label: FACT
findings.unit: USD per share from the gain

findings.claim: The USD 2.85 of clean Q2 EPS closely matches the USD 2.88 analyst consensus, confirming that the sell-side was forecasting operating earnings while the headline reported a 294% EPS increase. The gap between the two is entirely mark-to-market.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived: reported USD 9.11 less the company-disclosed USD 6.26, against the USD 2.88 consensus

findings.claim: Consequently the widely cited price/earnings ratio of about 17x — the basis for calling Alphabet the cheapest megacap — is computed on trailing earnings inflated by these gains. On estimated FY2026 operating earnings of roughly USD 11.37 per share the multiple is approximately 29.8x, not 17x.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived: FY2026E operating income ~USD 170bn less ~17% tax over 12.23bn shares; price USD 338.72

findings.claim: Return on capital cannot be measured meaningfully mid-cycle. The denominator is being rebuilt at roughly USD 200bn a year and the assets are not yet generating their full revenue, so any current ROIC reading is an artefact of timing rather than a statement about the business.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: Rate sensitivity has reversed with the capital structure. On approximately USD 142bn of net cash a 100bp rise still adds roughly USD 1.4bn of pre-tax income, but with debt roughly doubled and further issuance planned, the marginal effect of higher rates is now a rising funding cost on a multi-year borrowing programme rather than a windfall on idle cash.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived: 142,000 x 1%; debt trajectory from the 2025-26 issuance record

risks.text: The most widely cited valuation statistic for this company — a ~17x P/E — is wrong for investment purposes, being computed on earnings that include USD 77bn of after-tax paper gains. Anyone who owns Alphabet because it is 'the cheap megacap' owns it on a false premise.
Free cash flow has gone negative and the company is funding capex with debt and the largest equity raise in US corporate history while still paying a dividend.
Depreciation on short-lived compute assets will rise sharply and could compress reported operating margin even as revenue compounds.
The buyback that supported the share count has stopped, and issuance is diluting it instead.

catalysts.text: Q3 2026 results — whether free cash flow stays negative and whether buybacks resume

conclusions: The single most important finding in this dossier: Alphabet's headline ~17x P/E is computed on trailing earnings containing USD 77.1bn of after-tax unrealised gains on SpaceX and one private holding. On clean FY2026 operating earnings the multiple is approximately 29.8x. Alphabet is not the cheapest megacap; it is priced in line with the market's growth cohort.
Alphabet disclosed this reconciliation itself — the USD 6.26 per share of gain inside the USD 9.11 reported. The distortion is in the market's summary statistic, not in the company's reporting.

The capital structure has inverted completely in one year: buybacks halted from USD 28.3bn, an USD 84.75bn equity raise launched, long-term debt roughly doubled to USD 98bn, and free cash flow negative for the first time since the 2004 IPO.

There is no solvency question — roughly USD 142bn of net cash and USD 170bn of operating income — but there is now a genuine funding question, and the company is answering it by selling stock while paying a dividend.
Return on capital cannot be measured mid-cycle and will not be measurable for several years. That is not a neutral observation: it means the central claim of the bull case is currently unfalsifiable.
thesisImpact: Phase 4 changes the valuation question entirely. Phases 1-3 built a strong operating case; Phase 4 establishes that the multiple the market quotes for this business is roughly half the real one, and that the company is now funding itself the way a capital-intensive utility does. The Phase 5 work must be done on clean earnings, must weight the DCF down because near-term free cash flow is negative, and must treat depreciation policy as the principal sensitivity.
